# Large-maximum simplex normals: exact conditioning removes the one-vertex restriction

This theorem extends the counting result in
`candidate bbd9056fa863fc6b`. The other
normal coefficients are arbitrary. The remaining untreated positive
normals have every coefficient strictly below 2/(d+1).

## Theorem

Let d>=1, T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), V=|T|, and Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.
Let r_h=R-alpha*h>=0 for h=0,...,m, where R>0 and alpha>=0. Take
the fiber r_h T at each of the two integer bases -h and h+1. Fix
u_i>=0 with sum_i u_i=1, and suppose

    M=max_i u_i >= 2/(d+1).                              (1)

For EVERY beta>=0, the closed halfspace

    -beta z+u.x>=R/(d+1)

through the actual centroid of the fiber at base zero has mass at
least Gamma_d/2 times the total mass of the paired chain. The same
conclusion holds for every finite concave nonincreasing radius chain
by the proved exact affine-radius reduction.

Only (1) is imposed on the positive normal. In particular, another
coefficient may exceed 1/(d+1) or equal M. No classification into
equal-coordinate groups is used.

## 1. The exact conditional simplex law

Permute coordinates so u_1=M. For a uniform point X in T, put W=X_1.
The usual slice Jacobian, or direct integration of the simplex, gives
the following independent representation:

    W has density d(1-w)^(d-1) on [0,1],
    Y=(X_2,...,X_d)/(1-W) is uniform on T_(d-1),
    X=(W,(1-W)Y).

For d=1, the second simplex consists of the single point and the
remaining projection below is Z=0. Define

    Z=sum_(j=2)^d u_j Y_j.

Then u.X=MW+(1-W)Z. One has 0<=Z<M almost surely. Indeed Z<=M
because sum Y_j<=1; equality requires Y to belong to a proper face
on which sum Y_j=1 and every positive coordinate corresponds to a
coefficient M. This has (d-1)-volume zero whenever d>=2. For d=1,
Z=0<M=1. Thus repeated maximal coefficients create no atom requiring
a special averaging argument.

Conditional on Z, the normalized cap probability at a threshold v is

    P(u.X>=v | Z)
       = min{1, ((M-v)_+/(M-Z))^d}.                     (2)

For v<=Z this is one; for Z<v<M it follows by integrating the exact
Beta(1,d) tail of W; and for v>=M it is zero, up to null endpoints.
If desired, the irrelevant value on Z=M can be defined by its limiting
step function. All conditional probabilities are bounded by one.

## 2. Easy tilts

Put tau=1/(d+1), t=R*tau, and

    F_r(s)=|rT intersect {u.x>=s}|/V.

If beta>=alpha*tau, then t-beta*h<=tau*r_h. Thus every left cap
contains the halfspace cap through its own fiber centroid. The ordinary
Grünbaum inequality gives F_(r_h)(t-beta*h)>=Gamma_d*r_h^d. Summing
proves the result. This includes alpha=0; zero-radius fibers have zero
d-volume. The case m=0 also follows from its left cap alone.

## 3. Hard tilts and exact clipped power lists

Assume alpha>0 and 0<=beta<alpha*tau. Normalize the continuous
coordinates by R, and set

    a=alpha/R,
    theta=1-tau/M,
    b=beta/(M*alpha),
    rho_h=1-ah.

Condition (1) gives theta>=1/2, while the tilt condition gives
0<=b<1-theta. Also theta<1 because tau>0. Define the same two lists
as in the proved counting lemma:

    L_h=1-a(1-b)h/theta,
    B_h=1-ab/theta-a(1+b)h/theta.

For every h in the finite prefix,

    (L_h)_+<=rho_h,       (B_h)_+<=rho_h.                 (3)

For the first inequality, 1-b>=theta. For the second,
1+b>=theta and its initial value is at most one. The radii rho_h
are nonnegative by assumption.

For almost every Z, put

    C_Z=(M-tau)/(M-Z)>0.

Substitution into (2), with no change of normal or tilt, gives the
two EXACT normalized fiber caps

    F_(r_h)(t-beta*h)/R^d
         = E[min{rho_h^d, C_Z^d (L_h)_+^d}],
    F_(r_h)(t+beta*(h+1))/R^d
         = E[min{rho_h^d, C_Z^d (B_h)_+^d}].            (4)

The formulas remain true if rho_h=0, with both sides zero. They do
not replace the actual law of Z by a moment condition or a chosen
point. In particular, they retain all effects of the remaining normal
coefficients.

If C_Z<=1, (3) makes the minima in (4) equal to their second entries.
The exact two-list counting lemma with exponent d therefore gives

    sum_h [min{rho_h^d,C_Z^d(L_h)_+^d}
            +min{rho_h^d,C_Z^d(B_h)_+^d}]
       >= C_Z^d sum_h rho_h^d.

If C_Z>=1, (3) instead gives

    min{rho_h^d,C_Z^d(L_h)_+^d}>=(L_h)_+^d,
    min{rho_h^d,C_Z^d(B_h)_+^d}>=(B_h)_+^d.

The same counting lemma then gives the lower bound sum_h rho_h^d.
Combining the two cases, for almost every Z the paired sum is at least

    min{1,C_Z^d} sum_h rho_h^d.                          (5)

All sums are finite and the conditional terms are bounded, so averaging
(5) and using (4) is immediate. Crucially, by (2),

    E[min{1,C_Z^d}]=F_1(tau),

the ACTUAL cap fraction through the centroid of the unit simplex in
the original direction u. The ordinary Grünbaum inequality gives
this expectation >=Gamma_d. Hence

    sum_h [F_(r_h)(t-beta*h)+F_(r_h)(t+beta*(h+1))]
       >=Gamma_d sum_h r_h^d.

The chain's exact total volume is 2V sum_h r_h^d, which proves the
claimed Gamma_d/2 fraction for its original halfspace and center.

## 4. Endpoint and transfer checks

At M=2/(d+1), theta=1/2 and the counting lemma includes this endpoint.
At beta=0, b=0 and all displayed formulas remain valid. At the boundary
beta=alpha/(d+1), the easy-tilt proof applies; no limit is needed.
Repeated maxima only give a null face Z=M, as checked in Section 1.
Zero other coefficients, zero final radii, and any finite prefix are
already allowed by (2)--(5) and the counting lemma.

For a concave nonincreasing radius profile, invoke the exact same-cap
reduction in
`candidate cebdfbe6dc0c0994`.
It preserves the central fiber, actual center, original normal, tilt,
bases, and number of fiber pairs while weakly decreasing the deficit.
The affine deficit just proved is nonnegative, so the original deficit
is nonnegative. Thus the theorem applies to all such concave chains
in the normal range (1).

This does not treat all bounded-coefficient normals M<2/(d+1), and it
does not assert a mixed-integer center result for general convex bodies.
